operator_chain.notes: focalDistance drives focus plane
enable Depth Buffer output

common_pitfalls: focaldist must be in scene units, not pixels
fstop below 1.0 produces unrealistic bokeh

operator_chain.notes: focaldist parameter driven by LFO or animation CHOP
slow sine wave between near and far subject distances
enable Depth Buffer output for post-process DoF

common_pitfalls: Export the lfoCHOP channel directly to cameraCOMP focaldist via CHOP export or python expression
LFO type 0 is sine — use a slow freq (0.1–0.3 Hz) for cinematic rack pacing
Racking too fast looks mechanical; ease in/out with a lagCHOP after the LFO

operator_chain.notes: uniform Gaussian blur across entire image, small radius for dreamy softness
operand=over with alpha mix to preserve detail

common_pitfalls: A large radius without compositing back destroys detail — keep size under 8 or blend
Increasing passes is cheaper than a single very large radius for smooth results
For a full diffusion glow effect blend with screen instead of over

operator_chain.notes: lift black point to isolate brights
wide radius, multi-pass
operand=add

common_pitfalls: Without lumaLevel isolation the entire image blurs, not just highlights
Add operand on Composite TOP must be set explicitly, default is over

operator_chain.notes: high blacklevel extracts lens flare sources
scale Y < 1 to simulate anamorphic squeeze on the flare layer
set blur direction to horizontal only, large X radius
operand=add or screen

common_pitfalls: blurTOP direction parameters are dirx/diry as normalized vectors — set diry to 0 for pure horizontal streak
Squeeze must happen before blur, not after, or the streak will be circular
Blue tint the streak layer with a levelTOP to replicate anamorphic blue lens character

operator_chain.notes: lift blacks slightly, reduce white ceiling for filmic contrast roll-off
load a 1D or 3D LUT texture for filmic tone mapping

common_pitfalls: lookupTOP expects the LUT image in the second input — a horizontal 1D gradient image mapped to output colors
For a 3D LUT use a cube-strip texture and set the Lookup TOP to 3D mode
Apply grading in linear light before any gamma correction, then add a gammaCorrectTOP at the end

operator_chain.notes: render with a bright occluder/light source visible
multi-tap radial blur centered on light source screen position
operand=add, control intensity with level

common_pitfalls: The GLSL shader needs the light source screen-space UV position as a uniform — pass it via a glslTOP uniform parameter
Too many samples (>128) tanks GPU performance — 32–64 is the cinematic sweet spot
Mask out the occluder shape before the radial blur so rays don't bleed through solid geometry

operator_chain.notes: enable Velocity output in render TOP for depth-aware motion vectors
sample along per-pixel velocity vector for physically correct motion blur
blend amount controls shutter-angle effect

common_pitfalls: renderTOP must output a velocity pass — check the Render TOP Buffers page for the velocity output toggle
Velocity vectors are in clip space; scale by shutterscale uniform to control blur length
Static geometry with fast camera moves still needs velocity computed from camera matrix delta per frame

operator_chain.notes: output separate R, G, B planes for independent offset
small translate on R channel away from center
small opposite translate on B channel toward center
merge offset R, original G, offset B back to RGB

common_pitfalls: Offset is in UV space (0–1 range) — values above 0.01 look like a glitch, not a lens aberration
Apply the effect only at frame edges using a radial mask composited with the aberrated version
Use two separate transformTOPs for R and B with opposite signs — do not try to offset G

operator_chain.notes: monochrome noise, small amplitude, re-seed each frame for temporal variation
shift noise range from 0–1 to -0.5–0.5 for additive overlay
operand=add at low opacity; screen operand for brighter grain character

common_pitfalls: Static noise looks like a texture, not grain — drive noiseTOP seed with absTime.frame for per-frame variation
Grain amplitude above 0.12 reads as heavy VHS noise rather than clean film grain
Use a screenCHOP or math to keep output in 0–1 range after addition to avoid clipping bright areas
